criteria.text: Patient has one of the five diagnoses listed in Criteria for Approval.
Prescriber is affiliated with the regional Hemophilia Treatment Center.
Enrolled Alaska Medicaid prescribing and dispensing providers agree to comply with the standards of care in this and affiliated Hemophilia Factor Program documents.
Submitted treatment plan defines prophylactic and on-demand regimens, infusion intervals, and number of doses to be dispensed per fill.

Partial encoding of Alaska Medicaid Hemophilia Factor Program: Version 1; Approved 11/17/17; PDF Effective 5/1/2019. The stub effective_date 2017-01-01 is preserved; appendix footers still say Effective pending.

Encoded: only the five Criteria for Approval bullets: closed diagnosis list, regional HTC affiliation, enrolled prescribing/dispensing provider SOC agreement, defined prophylactic and on-demand treatment plan including infusion intervals and doses per fill, and continued infusion logging. No age, severity, inhibitor-status, specialty, or prior-therapy gates are added.

Authorizations (notes only): initial up to 3 months; reauthorization may be longer with required clinical documentation and established clinical stability. Authorizations are patient/prescriber/pharmacy-specific; changes require formal transfer. Emergency one-time transfer overrides may be requested through the Clinical Call Center if delay could adversely affect patient health.

Quantity (notes only): based on treatment plan, no more than one month supply; prophylactic and on-demand product must not be combined in the same claim; dispensing tolerance ±5%. max_units is null; quantity enforcement requires manual review.

Provider/Facility Adherence and Required Documentation (notes only): all program requirements apply to enrolled providers. Prescriber-signed intake/treatment plan and new-patient, annual, and changed-information review include identifiers/contact information, demographics, height/weight, diagnosis/confirmation, baseline and on-regimen factor levels, severity, venous access, inhibitor status/date, allergies, both dosing regimens, prescriber and HTC. Individual intake items are not approval predicates.

Provider operations (notes only): regional/home HTC coordination, prescriber product selection and treatment responsibility, annual pharmacy notice by July 1, 24/7 pharmacist and emergency access, nursing access, home assessment, storage, inventory, waste disposal, education and communication/delivery needs. Pharmacy maintains infusion logs, reviews compliance/utilization variances, and supplies logs to the State on request.

Dispensing/delivery SOC (notes only): patient pharmacy choice and patient/caregiver-initiated fills, no auto fills, documented shipment authorization and stock on hand, one-month supply minus stock with five-day emergency supply allowance. Established-patient delivery within two days, new nonemergency delivery within three days, active-bleed delivery within 24 hours; cold chain, physical recipient signature, and NDC/lot/potency/expiration records are required.

Supply, purchasing/reporting and patient operations (notes only): access to all prescribed FDA-approved brands/assays/vial sizes, supplier lists and alternate pharmacy referral; incident reporting to prescriber/HTC within one business day; no outpatient billing for inpatient use; audit records and purchase invoices; recall notification system, notification within 24 hours when required/recommended, replacement prescription and retrieval/quarantine within seven days; counseling, no pharmacy-directed brand/dose selection or gifts, and required provider training/continuing education.

Appendices and forms (notes only): responsibility matrices, intake/treatment plan, pharmacokinetic monitoring, emergency stock, infusion logs, monthly/on-demand contacts and continuing education remain operational documentation. Remaining gaps: evidence verification, authorization/renewal/transfer, quantity logistics, all provider SOC operations, purchasing/reporting, forms and appendices require manual review.
